chunk_findings.detail: `max_events` can make `enforce` report `UNDER` after seeing only a prefix of the lane’s usage events, so a lane that has exceeded its cap is not stopped. Example: `budget_usd=10`, `warn_fraction=0.5`, and `driver.events(handle)` yields two `usage` events with costs `6` and `6`. With `max_events=1`, the loop processes the first cost (`spent=6`), then on the second usage event increments `seen` to `2`, breaks before adding the second cost, and returns `Verdict(UNDER, spent=6, cap=10)`. No `interrupt`/`stop` is called and no `lane.budget_stopped` record is written, even though the lane has actually spent `12` and should have been stopped. Because `max_events` is a public parameter, any caller that uses it to bound event reads gets a false under-budget verdict; a truncated enforcement pass should not be reported as `UNDER`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/budgetstop.py:enforce

chunk_findings.detail: `max_events` does not actually bound the number of events processed; it only counts `usage` events, contrary to its docstring (“stops collecting after that many events”). If `driver.events(handle)` yields an unbounded stream of non-usage events (for example, repeated `event="log"` events) and no `usage` events, `seen` is never incremented, so the `if max_events and seen > max_events: break` guard never fires. Given `max_events=1`, `enforce` still loops forever despite the caller requesting a bounded read, defeating the test/supervisor escape hatch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/budgetstop.py:enforce

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds a runtime budget-stop module and documents that the lane supervisor will interrupt a lane once its usage reaches `budget_usd`, but the manifest contains no production call site for that enforcement. The only runtime-adjacent production change is the new audit field `budget_stop_enabled` in `launch.py`, while `launch.py` itself explicitly says it does not stop the lane after admission. Given a running lane with `[swarm] budget_stop_enabled = true` and usage events whose summed `part.cost` exceeds the template `budget_usd`, nothing in the changed files imports or calls `budgetstop.enforce` from the scheduler/lane supervisor, so the lane can continue running unbounded despite the docs and audit note claiming the cap will be enforced.

A user or agent following this documented prompt has no new MCP capability to set a per-lane cap, so the documented workflow is not supported by the shipped change.

The item states that OpenCode usage events already carry `part.cost` and `part.tokens.total`, but the fake at line 45 (and the unreadable fake at line 128) emits `LaneEvent(..., "usage", {"cost": c})`. chunk_findings.detail: The `Verdict.warned` field is not preserved when enforcement becomes unenforceable after a soft warn has already been recorded. For example, with `budget_usd=10`, `warn_fraction=0.5`, and a lane emitting `usage` events with costs `6.0` and then a second `usage` event whose `fields` lacks `cost`, `enforce` emits `lane.budget_warned`, then emits `lane.cap_unenforced`, but returns `Verdict(outcome=cap_unenforced, warned=False, ...)` because `_unenforced` constructs `Verdict` without the current `warned` state. A caller that uses the returned verdict to decide whether a warn was already recorded will believe no warn occurred even though the log already contains one.

chunk_findings.detail: A non-finite cost is treated as readable and can silently bypass the cap. For example, if a `usage` event has `fields={"cost": float("nan")}` and `budget_usd=1.0`, `_usage_cost` returns `nan`, `spent` becomes `nan`, all `spent >= cap` comparisons are false, and `enforce` returns `Verdict(outcome=under_budget, spent=nan, ...)` without recording `lane.cap_unenforced`. This is a lane reported as under budget even though its cost cannot be used to enforce the cap, violating the “never silently uncapped” requirement.

chunk_findings.detail: The knob is introduced with `new = "true"` and `impact = "additive"`, but making the runtime stop default-on changes existing lane behavior because it uses `budget_usd` as a hard stop even though `launch.py` documents `budget_usd` as an admission estimate. Given an existing approved lane template with `budget_usd = 1.0` whose lane legitimately emits usage events totalling `1.2` and would otherwise finish, applying the upgrade defaults causes the supervisor to interrupt the lane at `1.0`, failing the lane. An operator relying on `impact = "additive"` to mean “no existing behavior changes” may auto-apply this and lose running lanes; this should be marked behavior/breaking or disabled by default unless a separate explicit cap field is introduced.

chunk_findings.detail: The test name and the acceptance criterion say unreadable usage should be reported as `cap_unenforced`, not stopped, but the test only asserts `h.interrupts == 0`. If `budgetstop.enforce` records `RECORD_UNENFORCED` and then also calls the lane's fallback `stop` (setting `h.stopped = True`) or records `RECORD_STOPPED`, the test still passes: `h.interrupts` remains `0`, the outcome can still be `CAP_UNENFORCED`, and the filtered `unenforced` list still has one entry. The test therefore cannot falsify a wrong implementation that stops a lane because its usage was unreadable; it should assert `h.stopped is False` and that no `RECORD_STOPPED` record was emitted.

chunk_findings.detail: The enforcement compares binary-float sums directly to the float cap. With the default `Params()` and `budget_usd=1.0`, if the lane emits ten `usage` events whose `fields["cost"]` is `"0.1"` (or `Decimal("0.1")`), `_usage_cost` converts each cost to `float` and `spent += step` accumulates to `0.9999999999999999`. The guard `if spent >= cap:` is therefore false, so `enforce` returns `UNDER` after the loop without calling `_interrupt` or recording `RECORD_STOPPED`, even though the lane’s true usage has reached the approved budget. A monetary cap should accumulate as `Decimal` or use an explicit tolerance; otherwise a lane can hit its cap and be reported under budget.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/budgetstop.py:enforce

chunk_findings.detail: The test only checks that exactly one `RECORD_WARNED` record and one interrupt occur; it does not verify that the warn happened at the configured `warn_fraction` rather than at the full budget. A wrong `B.enforce` implementation that ignores `params.warn_fraction` and records `RECORD_WARNED` only when it also records `RECORD_STOPPED` still passes this test: with `budget_usd=1.0`, `warn_fraction=0.5`, and costs `[0.6, 0.6]`, the first event stays under budget, the second crosses budget, and the implementation emits one warn plus one stop/interrupt. The test sees `len(warns) == 1` and `h.interrupts == 1`, so `budget_warn_fraction` could be dead while the test remains green.

chunk_findings.detail: `_usage_cost` is documented to return `None` when a usage cost cannot be read, but the `float(cost)` conversion only catches `TypeError` and `ValueError`. Given a canonical `usage` event whose `fields={"cost": 10 ** 400}` (or a similarly huge decimal/integer string), `float(cost)` raises `OverflowError`, so `enforce` propagates the exception instead of returning `Verdict(CAP_UNENFORCED, ...)`. The lane is therefore not reported cap-unenforced, and the enforcement pass dies rather than following the “usage unreadable => cap_unenforced” contract.

chunk_findings.detail: The new docs state that the supervisor sums a running lane’s `usage` events using `part.cost`. The canonical `LaneEvent` usage payload carries the cost at the top-level `cost` field; `part.cost` is the raw pre-mapped field that the shipped adapter maps to `fields.cost`. A driver author following this docs and emitting a canonical usage event with only `{"part": {"cost": 2.0}}` will cause `_usage_cost` to see no cost, so `enforce` accumulates zero, returns `UNDER`, and fails to interrupt a lane that has actually exceeded `budget_usd`.
